items.title: Switch to batched OSV queries for `uv audit`
items.reason: Introduced the positional query/result `zip` without checking response cardinality. It is the historical origin of the behavior, not an existing tracker for this failure.

items.title: Batch large OSV queries
items.reason: Refactored the same path into 1,000-query chunks while retaining the truncating `zip`. Its tests cover equal-length responses, not missing results.

items.title: uv audit fails with error decoding response body when OSV returns empty range events
items.reason: An adjacent malformed-OSV-data case. It produced a hard decoding error rather than a false clean result and was resolved upstream, so it is not a duplicate.

items.title: uv audit: specialize malformed OSV error
items.reason: The follow-up to astral-sh/uv#19492 explicitly retained hard failure for malformed OSV data because detecting service problems is important, supporting fail-closed behavior for this distinct defect.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. Literal searches covered `querybatch`, `query_identifiers`, `no known vulnerabilities`, `exit 0`, `results`, `queries`, and `service-url`. Conceptual searches covered false negatives, incomplete or truncated responses, empty results, response cardinality, malformed OSV data, proxies, service errors, and audit exit codes. Fix-oriented review covered OSV client history and the pull requests for batch querying, large-query chunking, malformed-record errors, and nonzero audit exits. No existing tracker or fix for mismatched query/result counts was found. The broad roadmap astral-sh/uv#18506 does not track response completeness; astral-sh/uv#19876 was ruled out because it concerned a pre-response TLS failure and was withdrawn; astral-sh/uv#18512 only covers nonzero exits for actual findings.

type_reason: Current source accepts any `results` length and pairs results with queries using a truncating `zip`. A short HTTP-200 response therefore silently omits dependencies and can produce a clean banner and exit 0 for an incomplete audit. This is source-confirmed incorrect behavior, and no open issue or pull request already tracks it.
summary: No duplicate was found. The closest items are the merged pull requests that introduced and later refactored the unchecked positional pairing, plus earlier malformed-OSV work establishing that invalid service data should fail closed.
draft_response: Confirmed—this is a bug. The current batch-response path accepts any `results` length and zips it with the pending queries, so a short response drops unmatched packages and can incorrectly render a clean audit with exit 0. A response missing entries cannot establish that those packages are vulnerability-free and should be treated as a service error. This is consistent with astral-sh/uv#19515, where malformed OSV data is intentionally surfaced rather than skipped. The next step is to reject unequal query/result counts and add regression coverage for short responses, including paginated and chunked batches.
